title: Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management: generative insights in Demand planning, with a trends metric at general availability
summary: Hold: the contributor data restrictions omit Microsoft's exception for users who also hold Demand Planning Manager or System Administrator roles. The briefing also overlooks Microsoft's documented tenant-level Copilot setting when saying no admin switch is documented.

claims.claim: The generative insights feature page names no licence.
claims.quote: Searched: '"generative insights" "Demand planning" "license"'; read learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/supply-chain/demand-planning/generative-insights in full. It names no licence.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no admin setting that can turn generative insights off while retaining Demand planning.
claims.quote: By default, the tenant-level setting that enables the deployment of Copilot bots in Dataverse environments is enabled. However, a tenant admin can disable this setting. If the setting is disabled, you can't use Copilot features in finance and operations apps.
claims.fix: Replace the broad no-admin-switch assertions with: 'The feature page documents no generative-insights-specific switch. Microsoft documents a tenant-level Publish bots with AI features setting and states that disabling it prevents use of Copilot features in finance and operations apps; its feature table includes Generative insights for Demand planning.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/fin-ops-core/dev-itpro/copilot/enable-copilot. Narrow the open question to a switch specific to generative insights, without treating licences and roles as the only documented controls.

claims.claim: Demand Planning Contributor grants Demand planning access and permits viewing worksheets and editing accessible data.
claims.quote: Grants access to Demand planing. View worksheets (see shared worksheets and save their own views). Controlled by row-level access and can edit data they have access to.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Demand Planning Manager is a Demand planning access role.
claims.quote: Demand Planning Manager ... Grants access to Demand planning and all features that are available to the Demand Planning Contributor role.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: System Administrator grants Demand planning access.
claims.quote: Grants access to Demand planning and all features that are available to the Demand Planning Manager, Demand Planning Contributor, and Basic User roles.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Row-level access rules restrict every Demand Planning Contributor to explicitly granted rows.
claims.quote: Users who have the Demand Planning Contributor role (but not Demand Planning Manager or System Administrator) can access Demand planning, but they can only view and edit data that they're granted access to.
claims.fix: Qualify each statement about contributor row-level restrictions in Risk assessment, Scope and the Before rollout checklist with 'who do not also hold Demand Planning Manager or System Administrator'. In Scope use: 'Contributors who do not also hold Demand Planning Manager or System Administrator can view and edit only data granted by row-level access rules.' The cited security roles page explicitly excludes those two additional roles.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The generative insights feature page does not describe whether generated insight results are restricted to the requesting user's rows.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Demand planning" "generative insights" "row" security permissions'; read the feature, Responsible AI FAQ and users-access pages. The feature page gives no generated-output row-filtering guarantee; the security page describes general contributor data access.

claims.claim: Licence assignment is available in Microsoft 365 admin center at Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page. Select a product. On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense assigns or removes a user's licences.
claims.quote: Add or remove licenses for the user to enable or disable their use of Microsoft cloud offerings that the company has licenses to. POST /users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense
claims.fix: Keep the endpoint unchanged: the cited v1.0 reference supports it, so the deterministic path-string warning is not a fault. Add to the row note: 'The request body uses addLicenses to specify licences to add and removeLicenses to specify licence skuIds to remove; removeLicenses is required and can be empty.'

claims.claim: Licence assignment in Microsoft 365 admin center requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: The Demand planning licensing page links licence-assignment guidance but does not itself name the Graph assignLicense call.
claims.quote: Searched: '"generative insights" "Demand planning" "license"'; read demand-planning/demand-planning-licensing and graph/api/user-assignlicense. The licensing page links Assign licenses and Microsoft 365 admin-center assignment, but names no Graph operation.

claims.claim: Direct user security roles are managed in Power Platform admin center at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Manage security roles.
claims.quote: Select Manage. In the Manage pane, select Environments, and then select an environment from the list. Select Settings. Select Users + permissions, and then select Users. On the Users page select a user, and then select Manage security roles.

claims.claim: Demand planning row-level access rules are located at Configuration > Row level access.

claims.claim: The documented procedure for setting up row-level security uses a system admin account.

claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly say whether the Supply Chain Management Demand Planning Feature management switch governs generative insights.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Demand planning" "generative insights" disable enable admin feature management'; read install-demand-planning and fin-ops-core/dev-itpro/copilot/enable-copilot. The latter says insights are enabled on installation, but neither maps them to the SCM Feature management switch.

claims.claim: The listed licence and security-role controls govern Demand planning app access rather than being generative-insights-specific switches.
claims.quote: To be able to access Demand planning, users must sign in a Power Platform user account that has the security roles for the features they need.

claims.claim: The prepare action rating fits the standard for the verified default, target and risk.
claims.quote: action: "prepare"; risk: "medium"; targetDate: "January CY2027"; defaultState: "on". The standard counts a month-only target from its first day and calls for act-now within about 60 days when risk or cost is medium or higher.
claims.fix: Set action to 'act-now'. January 1, 2027 is 43 days after the supplied November 19, 2026 run date; the roadmap enables the feature automatically and the page rates risk medium and identifies pre-rollout access and communication decisions.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks administrators to review appears in the controls table.
claims.quote: Review the row-level access rules that limit what each Demand Planning Contributor can see ... The controls table lists only licence assignment and security-role assignment.
claims.fix: The Before rollout step asking administrators to review row-level access rules has no corresponding controls-table row. Remove that checklist step; the existing prose about where row-level rules live can remain. Do not add a control row as part of this correction.
